fact: ITWeb Africa reports Malawi launched its web-based Land Information Management System in February 2024, where registered users submit documents, receive notifications and pay ground rent and application fees, while some transactions remain manual.
The Ministry of Lands is reviewing LIMS workflows and developing digital procedures to move the remaining manual land transactions onto the platform, per a ministry deputy director of LIMS.

The Digital Malawi Acceleration Project reports 647 District Land Officers trained nationwide on LIMS and the Ministry equipped with over 400 computers, 100+ printers and four GNSS/GPS units, with LIMS optimization still under discussion with the World Bank mission.
The Ministry of Lands says it is implementing the Land Information Management System with the World Bank's AGCOM project, with a contract signed 10 May 2021 for a 20-month rollout through to go-live.
President Chakwera launched the Land Information Management System (LIMS) on 29 February 2024; the article does not say transactions are processed in it.

Malawi Broadcasting Corporation reported on 29 February 2024 that the Ministry of Lands' Land Information Management System (LIMS) was being launched, with an online portal for land-related transactions including registry.
Malawi's Lands Minister said in an interview that the ministry has digitalised lease approvals and is comparing physical files with its Land Information Management System.
Lands Minister Chimwemwe Chipungu said on 12 August 2026 that the ministry is currently digitising land administration processes via a Land Information Management System (LIMS).
The Ministry of Agriculture's spokesperson says the Land Information Management System (LIMS) has been used to register about 130,000 customary land parcels, and AGCOM II is supporting its upscaling.

Malawi's Minister of Lands said at a Zomba training for lands officers and registrars that the Land Information Management System (LIMS) has been introduced and lets Malawians access land information digitally.

247Malawi reports the Ministry of Lands has launched the Land Information Management System (LIMS) to manage land issues and track land transactions in Blantyre, under the World Bank-funded Digital Malawi Acceleration Project.
